message.content:
Investigate this repository (working dir /bench/repo) to answer these questions about the caching layer:

1. Is there any Redis connection configured anywhere for a cache layer? Search for "redis", "Redis", "ioredis", "REDIS_URL", cache client setup, etc.
2. Where and how is the cache layer actually configured/implemented? Look for cache modules, cache clients, in-memory caches, LRU, etc.
3. Is there any TTL (time-to-live) applied to "user" entries or user caching specifically? Search for TTL, expiry, maxAge, cache.set with user, etc.

Report exact file paths and line numbers for anything you find. If Redis is NOT used, say so explicitly and describe what the actual caching mechanism is. Be thorough — check package.json/dependency manifests, config files, and source code.

attachment.content:
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

content.text:
I have a complete picture. No further searches needed.

## Findings

### 1. Redis: NOT used anywhere
There is no Redis connection, client, or configuration in this repository. I searched exhaustively for `redis`, `Redis`, `ioredis`, `REDIS_URL` across all source, config, and dependency manifests:
- Not in the Go dependency manifest `/bench/repo/go.mod` (no `go-redis`, `redigo`, etc.)
- Not in `/bench/repo/web/package.json` (no `ioredis`, `node-cache`, etc.)
- Not in any `.go`, `.ts`, `.js`, `.env`, `.yml`/`.yaml` file, nor `go.sum`

This is the Memos application. The backend is Go; the web frontend is React/TypeScript.

### 2. The actual caching mechanism: a custom in-memory cache (Go `sync.Map` + TTL)

The cache layer is a hand-written, thread-safe in-memory cache. There is no external cache store.

- Implementation: `/bench/repo/store/cache/cache.go`
  - `Cache` struct backed by `sync.Map` with an `atomic.Int64` item counter (lines 66-73).
  - Each entry (`item`, lines 34-39) stores `value`, an `expiration time.Time`, and an estimated `size`.
  - `Interface` defines `Set`, `SetWithTTL`, `Get`, `Delete`, `Clear`, `Size`, `Close` (lines 10-32).
  - A background goroutine (`cleanupLoop`/`cleanup`, lines 199-250) periodically evicts expired entries on `CleanupInterval`; `Get` also lazily evicts expired entries on access (lines 135-144).
  - `cleanupOldest` (lines 253-313) enforces the `MaxItems` cap by evicting ~20% of the oldest entries when the count exceeds the limit. Note: it is size/count-bounded and TTL-bounded, but it is not a strict LRU (eviction is by expiration time, not last-access recency).
  - `DefaultConfig()` (lines 56-64): DefaultTTL 10m, CleanupInterval 5m, MaxItems 1000.

- Cache wiring / configuration: `/bench/repo/store/store.go`
  - `Store` holds three caches: `instanceSettingCache`, `userCache`, `userSettingCache` (lines 27-29).
  - `New()` builds a hardcoded `cache.Config` (lines 40-45: DefaultTTL 10m, CleanupInterval 5m, MaxItems 1000, no eviction callback) and instantiates all three caches with it (lines 51-53). These config values are hardcoded, not driven by env vars or config files.
  - `Close()` stops all three cache goroutines (lines 73-76).

- Cache key helpers: `/bench/repo/store/user.go` line 88 (`userCacheKey` = user ID as string) and `/bench/repo/store/cache.go` lines 7-9 (`getUserSettingCacheKey` = `"<userID>-<key>"`).

- Frontend (separate, client-side) caching uses TanStack Query, not Redis: `/bench/repo/web/src/lib/query-client.ts` and `/bench/repo/web/src/components/MemoEditor/services/cacheService.ts`. This is browser in-memory query caching, unrelated to any server cache.

### 3. TTL applied to "user" entries

There is a TTL on user entries, but it is NOT user-specific — users get the shared default TTL.

- All user writes go through `s.userCache.Set(...)`, which calls the plain `Set` method. `Set` (`/bench/repo/store/cache/cache.go` lines 92-95) delegates to `SetWithTTL` using `c.config.DefaultTTL`. No call site ever uses `SetWithTTL` with a custom duration for users.
- Therefore user entries expire after the DefaultTTL of 10 minutes, configured in `/bench/repo/store/store.go` line 41 (`DefaultTTL: 10 * time.Minute`).
- User cache `Set` call sites (all default TTL): `/bench/repo/store/user.go` lines 98, 122, 132, 143, 167.
- User cache reads: `/bench/repo/store/user.go` line 150 (`GetUser` checks cache by ID first).
- User cache invalidation on delete: `/bench/repo/store/user_delete.go` lines 39-40 (`deleteUserCache` -> `s.userCache.Delete`), invoked from `/bench/repo/store/user.go` line 179.
- The same 10-minute default TTL also applies to `userSettingCache` (set at `/bench/repo/store/user_setting.go` lines 59, 78, 106) and `instanceSettingCache`.

The expiration itself is enforced in `SetWithTTL` (`cache.go` line 112, `expiration: time.Now().Add(ttl)`), checked in `Get` (line 135) and in the background `cleanup` (line 227).

### Summary
No Redis (or any external cache) is present. Caching is an in-process, TTL-based in-memory cache implemented in `/bench/repo/store/cache/cache.go` and instantiated with hardcoded config in `/bench/repo/store/store.go`. User entries are cached in `userCache` and expire under the shared default TTL of 10 minutes; there is no user-specific TTL override, and eviction is TTL + max-items based rather than strict LRU.
